policy: Owner-authorized 2026-10-28 automatic topic choice. Original editorial briefs written for this channel from the cited biblical passages; never competitor titles, scripts or artwork. Ranking uses only measured public demand (views per day across distinct channels) plus the stated season; it is an interest signal, not a forecast. Every brief still passes the unchanged factual, visual, voice, audio and final QA.

topics.topic: The Tower of Babel: the bricks, the plain of Shinar and the scattering in Genesis 11
topics.focus: What Genesis 11:1-9 says: one language, baked bricks and bitumen on the plain of Shinar, the city and tower, the confusion of speech and the scattering. Attribute any link to Mesopotamian ziggurats to scholars as comparison, not identification.

topics.topic: The Ark of the Covenant: how Exodus describes it, its capture and its road to Jerusalem
topics.query: Ark of the Covenant history mystery
topics.focus: The text's description of the chest, poles and cherubim, its capture by the Philistines, Dagon and the return, and David bringing it to Jerusalem. Never claim a modern location or discovery; later legends are labeled as legends.

topics.topic: David and Goliath: the valley of Elah standoff, the armor and the sling in 1 Samuel 17
topics.focus: The forty-day standoff, Goliath's described height and armor, David's sling and five stones, and the aftermath. Note that ancient manuscripts differ on Goliath's height and attribute that to textual scholarship.

topics.topic: The walls of Jericho: Rahab, seven days of marching and the fall of the city in Joshua 2 and 6
topics.focus: Rahab and the spies, the scarlet cord, the seven-day march with trumpets and the fall of the walls as the text tells it. Archaeological dating of Jericho is debated: mention the debate only as a debate and give no excavation dates or names absent from the sources.

topics.topic: Samson's strength: the vow, the lion, Delilah and the temple of Dagon in Judges 13-16
topics.query: Samson and Delilah Bible story explained
topics.focus: The Nazirite vow, the lion and the riddle, the foxes and the jawbone, Delilah and the final scene in Gaza, as the text tells them. Do not psychologize beyond the text; label interpretation.

topics.topic: Elijah on Mount Carmel: the drought, the fire contest and the still small voice in 1 Kings 18-19
topics.query: Elijah Mount Carmel Bible story explained
topics.focus: The drought, Obadiah, the contest with the prophets of Baal, the water-soaked altar and fire, then Elijah's flight to Horeb and the still small voice. Attribute miracles to the narrative.

topics.topic: The Queen of Sheba: her journey, her hard questions and Solomon's court in 1 Kings 10
topics.focus: Her journey with spices and gold, the hard questions, what she saw at Solomon's court and the gifts. The location of Sheba is debated by scholars; later Ethiopian and Arabian traditions are labeled as later traditions, not the biblical text.

topics.topic: Joseph in Egypt: the coat, the prison dreams and the reunion in Genesis 37-45
topics.query: Joseph in Egypt Bible history explained
topics.focus: The coat and the pit, the dreams in prison, Pharaoh's dreams and the seven years, Joseph's rise and the reunion with his brothers. Any comparison with Egyptian history is attributed to scholars and labeled as debated.

topics.topic: The ten plagues of Egypt: what Exodus 7-12 actually describes, plague by plague
topics.focus: The sequence of plagues from the Nile turned to blood to the death of the firstborn and the first Passover, as the text describes them. Naturalistic explanations proposed by some writers are labeled as speculation, never as proof or disproof.

topics.topic: Crossing the Red Sea: the pillar of cloud, the parted waters and the song in Exodus 13-15
topics.focus: The route away from Egypt, the pillar of cloud and fire, the crossing and the song of Moses and Miriam. The location and the Hebrew 'yam suph' are debated; attribute proposals to scholars.

topics.topic: What Jesus ate: bread, fish and the meals the Gospels actually describe
topics.query: what did Jesus eat daily life history
topics.focus: Meals the Gospels describe: loaves and fishes, grilled fish by the lake, broiled fish in Luke 24 and the Passover meal. Do not assert an exact daily diet; general first-century food customs are attributed to historians.

topics.topic: The first Christmas in the Gospels: the census, the manger, the shepherds and the magi in Luke 2 and Matthew 2
topics.query: the real Christmas story Bible history
topics.focus: What Luke 2 and Matthew 2 each say: the census and journey to Bethlehem, the manger, the shepherds, the star and the magi, and the flight to Egypt. Distinguish the two accounts and later nativity traditions; the date of the census is debated by scholars.

topics.topic: Ruth and Naomi: from Moab to Bethlehem, gleaning and the redeemer in the book of Ruth
topics.focus: The famine and the move to Moab, Ruth's vow, gleaning in Boaz's field, the threshing floor and the kinsman-redeemer, as the text tells them. Explain gleaning and redemption customs from the text itself.
chapters: Where you go, I will go

topics.topic: Esther in the Persian court: the contest, Haman's decree and the reversal in the book of Esther
topics.focus: Esther chosen as queen, Haman's decree, Mordecai's plea and the banquet that turns the plot. Historical identification of the Persian king is attributed to scholars; Purim is described as the text describes it.

topics.topic: Inside Solomon's Temple: cedar, gold and the Most Holy Place in 1 Kings 6-8
topics.focus: Materials and measurements the text gives, the cedar from Lebanon, the bronze pillars and sea, the Most Holy Place and the dedication. Do not claim archaeological remains of the building; label any reconstruction as reconstruction.

topics.topic: The Last Supper: the upper room, the meal and the night it began in the Gospels
topics.focus: Preparing the room, the meal, the bread and cup, the footwashing in John and the night in Gethsemane. Compare the Gospel accounts and attribute dating debates to scholars.

topics.topic: The Garden of Eden: the four rivers, the two trees and the way out east in Genesis 2-3
topics.focus: The garden, the four named rivers, the tree of life and the tree of knowledge, the serpent and the cherubim at the east. Proposed locations are attributed to scholars and labeled as speculation.

topics.topic: Who were the Nephilim? What Genesis 6 and Numbers 13 actually say
topics.query: who were the Nephilim Bible explained
topics.focus: The few verses that mention the Nephilim and the sons of God, and the spies' report in Numbers 13. Present interpretations (including later writings) as interpretations with their sources, and label speculation clearly; never present giants as historical fact.
